issues.reason: Coordination and plurals states that coordinated noun phrases are distributive by default — 'replicate the whole predication once per conjunct (verbal -> one event each)' — and one event carrying five Theme fillers is the collective encoding the same section reserves for reciprocal/aggregate predicates ('many events = distributive; one event with many agents = collective'), so the parse asserts a single joint recording eventuality the text does not mark.

'record' is not in the collective class (gather / meet / assemble / collide) and carries no together/jointly marker, so the grouped-plural doctrine applies — 'a distributive predicate also hands the predication to the group's members via a rule' — and the (Implication (PartOf $x sk_ledger_1) ...) emission is simply absent.

gaps_confirmed: a descriptive adjective on a BARE-KIND object filler ('notable events' as a non-specific kind-level object): both the fuse-vs-split rule and the plural distributive rule need a witness or group symbol to hang the modifier on, and a bare kind filler has neither, so fusing is the only route that does not drop the qualifier
new_gaps: a definite plural whose predicate is aggregate over the SET yet outside the closed collective class ('the ledgers record <five record-types>' means the ledger system as a whole covers these, not that every ledger records every category): the mandated per-member rule at strength 1.0 over-asserts, and the collective exemption is restricted to reciprocal/aggregate predicates, so neither licensed form states what the sentence says

verb-class / noun-kind symbol collision under lemmatization: the event class in (Member sk_record_1 record) and the head genus in (Inheritance apprentice_record record) are one symbol, so seeded member-inheritance makes any apprentice-record instance a member of the event class 'record' and it will match recording-event query patterns
defect_summary: For issue 0 the compliant form is five separate record events, one per coordinated object NP, each with (Agent $e sk_ledger_1) — the shared subject symbol reused, as in 'Bob and Alice ate the cake' — and its own single Theme plus the same decomposition atoms; for issue 1 it is the per-member rule (Implication (PartOf $x sk_ledger_1) (And (Member (sk_record $x) record) (Agent (sk_record $x) $x) (Theme (sk_record $x) <filler>))) at (STV 1.0 0.9) beside each group event, though the new gap above notes that form over-asserts for this content.
notes: Theme rather than Patient on a merely-recording verb and 'Council' as a capitalized common-noun modifier with no Name atom are both right, and the fused notable_event with its exposed gradable-adjective genus is acceptable improvisation in the confirmed gap territory.
